import ctypes

# Load libraries
ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

# Define GSL constants
GSL_SUCCESS = 0
GSL_FAILURE = -1

# Define gsl_combination structure
class gsl_combination(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("n", ctypes.c_size_t),
                ("k", ctypes.c_size_t),
                ("data", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t))]

def next_combination(current_combination, n):
    k = len(current_combination)
    if k == 0 or k > n:
        return None
    
    # Create combination object
    comb = gsl_combination()
    comb.n = n
    comb.k = k
    
    # Allocate and initialize data array
    data_arr = (ctypes.c_size_t * k)(*current_combination)
    comb.data = ctypes.cast(data_arr, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t))
    
    # Call gsl_combination_next
    result = gsl.gsl_combination_next(ctypes.byref(comb))
    
    if result == GSL_SUCCESS:
        return tuple(comb.data[i] for i in range(k))
    else:
        return None

def assert_test():
    # Test case 1: Normal next combination
    assert next_combination((0, 1, 2), 5) == (0, 1, 3)
    
    # Test case 2: Last combination returns None
    assert next_combination((2, 3, 4), 5) is None
    
    # Test case 3: Empty combination returns None
    assert next_combination((), 5) is None
    
    # Test case 4: Single element combination
    assert next_combination((3,), 5) == (4,)
    
    # Test case 5: k > n returns None
    assert next_combination((0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 5) is None
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
